<intent-contract>

## Intent

**Problem:** The shipped `epic` template's only human review gate (`stories.after`, generated by `pause_after_item_when: "story.done_checkpoint"`) fires before `e2e`, `push`, and `link` — so when the operator reviews work, the branch has not yet been pushed and they cannot run the code on their own machine. The `bmad-spec` Story Breakdown guidance currently asks spec authors to set `done_checkpoint` on individual stories, which is redundant once the epic tail provides a standard review gate.

**Approach:** Add an unconditional `done-checkpoint` human-gate step at the very end of `templates/epic.yaml` (after `link`) so every epic run parks with a real pushed branch and compare URL available for operator review. Update `bmad-spec/SKILL.md`'s Story Breakdown guidance to drop `done_checkpoint` from the non-final-story ask list and explain that the epic tail is the standard review point.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- AGENTS.md exemplar freeze (rule 6): `tests/unit/application/templates/fixtures/exemplars/epic.yaml` is NOT updated — the frozen-exemplar contract allows the shipped template to evolve without touching test fixtures; the graph tests (`test_graph_shipped.py`, `test_plan_shipped.py`, `test_shipped_templates.py`) continue to use the frozen exemplar unchanged
- The `pause_after_item_when: "story.done_checkpoint"` loop clause stays in the shipped template; removing it would change the DSL semantics for mid-epic pauses and is out of scope for this story
- The new step must validate cleanly through `validate.py` (smoke test: `test_every_shipped_file_seeds_clean`); `uses: checkpoint` with `gate: human` is already supported by the DSL (see `repo-init@1`'s `context-review` step)
- The smoke tests (`test_shipped_smoke.py`) must continue to pass unchanged; no existing test file may be modified
- No application code (Python/TypeScript) changes; this is a template + guidance change only

**Block If:** Any ambiguity about the checkpoint step ID or its position relative to other epic tail steps (e2e, push, link) that cannot be resolved from the story description alone.

**Never:**
- Do not update `tests/unit/application/templates/fixtures/exemplars/epic.yaml` (exemplar freeze holds)
- Do not modify any existing test file
- Do not change the shipped `story.yaml`, `initiative.yaml`, or `repo-init.yaml` templates
- Do not add application (Python/TypeScript) code for this story

</intent-contract>

**Execution (TDD order — test first, then implementation):**
- `backend-api/tests/unit/application/templates/test_epic_tail_order.py` -- CREATE first -- TDD test file; define a local `seeded()` helper using the same pattern as `test_shipped_smoke.py` (imports: `seed_shipped`, `load_shipped_templates`, `FakeTemplateVersionRepository`, `FakeUnitOfWork`, `TemplatePorts`, `FakeClock`; `SHIPPED_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5] / "templates"`); write one test function `test_epic_has_a_human_gate_reachable_from_push` that: loads the shipped epic template via `seeded()`, validates it, builds the graph with `build_template_graph`, finds nodes where `node.human` is True, builds an adjacency list from `graph.edges`, does a BFS/DFS from the `push` node, and asserts that at least one human-gate node id is reachable from `push` — this test MUST FAIL before `done-checkpoint` is added to the shipped template (currently the only human node is `stories.after`, which is an ANCESTOR of `push`, not a descendant)
- `templates/epic.yaml` -- ADD `done-checkpoint` step after `link` -- append as the final element of the top-level `steps:` list (after the `link` step block, maintaining the 2-space indent):
  ```yaml
    - id: done-checkpoint
      uses: checkpoint
      gate: human
  ```
  No `with:` block needed; `gate: human` makes it a human-gate (operator-parks) step; this is the exact pattern of `repo-init.yaml:34-35`'s `context-review` step
- `.agents/skills/bmad-spec/SKILL.md` -- UPDATE Story Breakdown section -- at the paragraph beginning "Either way, walk the capabilities and constraints with the user" (line ~136), in the sentence "For each story, ask the user for `spec_checkpoint`, `done_checkpoint`, and any `invoke_dev_with` note rather than defaulting them silently", remove `, `done_checkpoint`` so it reads "For each story, ask the user for `spec_checkpoint` and any `invoke_dev_with` note rather than defaulting them silently"; then after the existing spec-gate note sentence, append: "Similarly, the epic tail pushes the branch and records the compare link before a final `done-checkpoint` human gate — this is the standard operator review point; set `done_checkpoint: true` only on a story that needs an additional mid-loop pause before e2e and push."

- Given the shipped `templates/epic.yaml` with the `done-checkpoint` step added, when it is seeded and validated via `seed_shipped` and `validate()`, then the result has no errors and no unvalidated nodes

- Given `make test` run after the template change, then the new `test_epic_tail_order.py` test passes and all existing tests (including `test_shipped_smoke.py`, `test_shipped_templates.py`, `test_graph_shipped.py`, `test_plan_shipped.py`) continue to pass
- Given `make lint`, then all checks pass (ruff, mypy, import-linter, env-contract, test-pairs — the new test file has no paired source module since `templates/*.yaml` are not Python modules)
- Given the updated `bmad-spec/SKILL.md`, when the Story Breakdown section is read, then `done_checkpoint` does not appear in the list of fields to ask about for each story, and a note states that the epic tail `done-checkpoint` is the standard operator review point

## Design Notes

`done-checkpoint` is unconditional — it always fires at the end of every epic run, giving the operator a pushed branch and compare link to review before the run completes. The existing `pause_after_item_when: "story.done_checkpoint"` mechanism stays for stories that need an earlier mid-loop pause (before e2e and push), but guidance now explicitly says this is only for exceptional cases on a final story, not the default.

The frozen exemplar (`fixtures/exemplars/epic.yaml`) intentionally does NOT get the `done-checkpoint` step. The exemplar is a snapshot decoupled from the shipped file; the graph tests assert properties of that snapshot, and the snapshot is only updated under deliberate Operator authorization. The smoke tests cover the shipped template's structural validity independently.

The TDD test file checks the behavioral invariant "a human gate is reachable from push" (the BFS start is anchored to step ID `"push"`, which is documented in the test's docstring).
